subsystems.name: Raw magic-state source
subsystems.role: makes many noisy copies of the special state that unlocks a non-Clifford gate (the T state).
parts: surface-code patch to hold the state

subsystems.name: Distillation circuit
subsystems.role: consumes a block of noisy states and outputs fewer, cleaner ones.
parts: small stabiliser code block, such as a Reed-Muller code

subsystems.name: Logical qubit fabric
subsystems.role: hosts the factory: the physical qubits and their error-correcting patches.

subsystems.name: Decoders and classical control
subsystems.role: turn syndrome measurements into corrections fast enough to keep the factory running.

subsystems.name: Factory scheduler
subsystems.role: decides how many distillation stages, how many patches, and when distilled states are shipped to the algorithm.

buildSteps.title: Fix the target
buildSteps.detail: Decide the gate the algorithm needs and the output error it can tolerate, for example going from about one error in a thousand raw states to one in a billion.

buildSteps.title: Choose a protocol
buildSteps.detail: Pick a small stabiliser code whose transversal operations act as the required gate — the 15-to-1 Reed-Muller scheme, introduced by Bravyi and Kitaev in 2005, is the classic choice.

buildSteps.title: Compile it fault-tolerantly
buildSteps.detail: Express every operation in the protocol as Clifford gates and measurements that the underlying error-correcting code can perform safely.

buildSteps.title: Design state injection
buildSteps.detail: Prepare a single physical qubit in the magic state and grow or merge a code patch around it, so the encoded state inherits only the physical error.

buildSteps.title: Simulate under noise
buildSteps.detail: Run Monte Carlo simulations across realistic error rates to check the output error and the success rate, and tune the number of rounds.

buildSteps.title: Lay out the factory
buildSteps.detail: Allocate code patches and a time schedule for each distillation stage; size the classical decoder to keep up in real time.

buildSteps.title: Run and recycle
buildSteps.detail: Operate the factory: feed in raw states, discard blocks that fail syndrome checks, and route good distilled states to the algorithm.

buildSteps.title: Shrink the overhead
buildSteps.detail: Revisit the protocol using newer schemes — growing a magic state directly inside a code patch, or catalyzed conversions between state types — to cut the qubit cost.

prerequisites.why: if adding qubits makes errors worse, no amount of distillation helps; small surface-code experiments now show error suppression as the code grows.
distillation circuits are built only from operations that are cheap and naturally fault-tolerant.
the whole chain is only as good as the raw states it starts from.
decoders must keep pace with measurement rounds, or the logical qubits idle.

prerequisites.tech: Qubit counts in the thousands to millions
prerequisites.why: factories can demand many times more qubits than the calculation they support.

pathway.milestone: below-threshold error correction in small hardware experiments; distillation studied mainly by simulation
pathway.unlocks: confidence that logical qubits can be made good enough to distil from.

pathway.milestone: injection plus one distillation round demonstrated end to end on hardware
a full fault-tolerant non-Clifford gate using a distilled state
pathway.unlocks: a universal logical gate set, the gate to genuinely useful quantum algorithms.

pathway.milestone: optimised factories — cultivation and catalyzed protocols — shrink qubit cost by roughly an order of magnitude
pathway.unlocks: logical machines large enough to run chemistry and materials calculations.
